item.title: Henley Anderson shines bright for Texas volleyball despite the 'ring of fire'
item.description: Texas Longhorns outside hitter Henley Anderson (22) takes the court ahead of the game against Alabama in Gregory Gym on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Despite being a freshman for Texas volleyball this season, Henley Anderson has had to maneuver a "ring of fire," according to her coach. After outside hitter Abby Vander Wal suffered an ACL injury at the end of August, Anderson has had to fill her role since the third game of the season. Jerritt Elliott recognizes just how difficult that can be for a first-year player. "When you're freshmen, the pressure and everything else you go through, it's really hard to kind of perform at a high level and it's overwhelming," Elliott said in August. Henley showed power and potential early, but she had to deal with a steep learning curve as Texas played seven top-25 teams before conference play. Plus she had to get used to being a main scoring option for the Longhorns with outside hitters Torrey Stafford and Cari Spears . Elliott kept telling her to "go be Henley Anderson" and as SEC play has gone on, the Dripping Springs product has settled in nicely. UP NEXT NO. 13 TEXAS VS. MISSOURI When/where: 7 p.m. Friday in Columbia, Mo. TV: SEC Network+. In Sunday's win over A&M , Anderson had 10 kills and hit .444 in the Longhorns' sweep, which earned her a third SEC freshman of the week accolade. Elliott said he has seen her grow in a short time. "Early in the year she was just a one-trick pony," Elliott said Sunday. "Now she's doing a lot of different things: adding tips and high-line shots, learning how to tool the block, hitting deep corner, hitting hard cross. She's starting to learn how to be a real volleyball player." MORE: ‘Like playing with MJ': Nya Bunton bided time behind greats. Will it help 2026 Longhorns? Anderson had a career-high 15 kills in the five-set match against SMU . She had seven kills against Wisconsin and combined for 12 in the first pair of SEC games. As the conference slate has continued, she's up to 11.2 kills per match through the last nine games and is becoming a dangerous part of No. 13 Texas' rotation. Georgia's Gigi Artiles is the only other outside hitters to be named the freshman of the week at least once. item.description: Quarterback Kyair Carr hopes to lead Troy to a Class A title. (Jim Franco/Times Union) The Section 2 Class A football playoffs start Friday with semifinal play. Out of the four programs remaining, two of them experienced losing seasons in 2025. The Super Bowl is set to take place Nov. 13 at Colonie High School. Here is a breakdown of the 2026 Class A playoffs. Semifinal matchups No. 4 Mohonasen (5-4) at No. 1 Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake (9-0), Friday, 7 p.m. No. 3 Queensbury (5-4) at No. 2 Troy (7-2), Friday, 7 p.m. Things to know Mohonasen enters the playoffs with its first five-win season since 2005. The program has dropped nine straight playoff games, starting with a 41-20 Class A semifinal loss to Averill Park in 2005. The last eight losses came in quarterfinal contests in eight-team sectional fields. Overall, Mohonasen is 3-13 in its sectional history, which began in 1996, including consecutive losses against Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake in 2011 (47-6), 2012 (68-6) and 2013 (67-8). … Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake finished 4-6 in 2025, bowing out in the quarterfinals. The Spartans (9-0) last won nine games in 2021 and seek their first 10-win season since 2017. … Troy is 3-0 against Queensbury in sectional semifinal contests. Overall, the Flying Horses own a 9-4 record against the Spartans in all meetings. … Queensbury is making its third straight semifinal appearance. Troy defeated the Spartans 39-16 in the 2025 semifinals. Player to watch There are a number of weapons that opponents must contend with when facing the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake offense. In particular, junior Talon Immel has provided many memorable moments for the Spartans this season at running back. Immel, a recent University at Albany men's lacrosse commit who missed two games earlier this season while competing for the 17-and-under USA national lacrosse team, delivered a season-best 165 yards and two touchdowns in a 28-6 win against Guilderland. item.title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 preview and predictions: Can Sami Zayn actually pull this off?
item.description: With no shortage of controversy in the build-up , WWE is moving forward with its annual Crown Jewel event this Saturday in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Featuring two champion vs. champion clashes, a last man standing match and a tag-team title bout, Crown Jewel has the potential to shake things up just weeks before Survivor Series: WarGames — and that isn't even factoring in both Money in the Bank briefcases, which are still waiting to be cashed in. As usual, to get you ready for the PLE, Uncrowned's Horsemen are here to answer several key questions and offer their predictions for the Saturday matinee. Let's ride! WWE appears determined to move forward with its Saudi plans, regardless of tensions within the region. ASSOCIATED PRESS 1. Sum up your thoughts on WWE's decision to keep Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. Does it impact your excitement or anticipation for the event? Robert Jackman: Where to start? I think this is a much more controversial decision than the call WWE made to run the original Crown Jewel in the wake of Jamal Khashoggi's killing back in 2018. Back then, WWE was defying what looked like a growing international boycott campaign. But as distasteful as it might have been to jet to Riyadh after a state-sanctioned killing of a dissident, Vince McMahon's WWE wasn't putting the whole company in the middle of an active warzone or defying any official travel advisories. As shocking as it is, this is exactly the sort of risk I had in mind when WWE made the big call to ramp up its Saudi partnership at the beginning of last year. Getting three times (at least) the revenue for your stadium shows without having to depend on pesky ticket sales sounds great on the face of it. But when you're taking a massive chunk of your event revenue from a single buyer, one that just happens to be an absolute monarchy in one of the world's least stable regions, it looks very different. Does it dampen my excitement for Saturday's show? I mean, this is the Crown Jewel championship we're talking about here … the champion of champions. The prize position on the WWE podium. How could I not be excited for that, right? Sorry, just practicing my corporate spiel in case I ever get recruited by TKO to the dark side. Drake Riggs: It's stupid and unnecessary, yet entirely unsurprising. I haven't wasted too much energy on this whole debacle because WWE has been treading water for so long. But it's just annoying, and you hope for everyone's safety above all else. I still wish we would see a majority of the roster stick up for themselves and say no to these kinds of things as a collective unit. Theoretically, it should be much easier to do that in an industry like pro-wrestling compared to, let's say, MMA. That being said, the geopolitical situation doesn't change my overall excitement level for this card, which really only has a few things to look forward to anyway. item.title: Family thankful for support as De Miguel funeral held
item.description: Jesus de Miguel's funeral took place in the town of Navahermosa in Spain on Thursday [Reuters] Jesus de Miguel's family said "the mark he has left on so many people" is something they will always remember as the footballer's funeral took place on Thursday. The Tenerife forward, who was 30, died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second division match on Monday. After colliding with the FC Andorra goalkeeper, De Miguel lay motionless on the pitch while being treated by medical staff and was taken to hospital, where the father-of-one died at 07:00 GMT on Tuesday. Goalkeeper Jesus Owono was sent off for the challenge and the game was abandoned. In the hours after the death was announced, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez - the stadium on the island of Tenerife, where Monday's game took place. Tributes have been paid to De Miguel, who joined Tenerife in the summer of 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competitions this week. His agent, Manuel Hernandez, issued a statement on behalf of the family, which read: "Thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being with us. "We cannot find enough words to thank you for every message, every phone call and every gesture of affection we are receiving. "Thank you to everyone who has remembered him - his colleagues, friends, supporters and all the clubs that have sent us their condolences and stood by us during this deeply painful time. "Feeling such affection for Jesus and seeing the mark he has left on so many people is something we will always carry with us." In a statement issued by his club Andorra on Wednesday, goalkeeper Owono said he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life". "I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus," he added. "I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him." De Miguel's funeral was held in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa, Toledo, about 125km from the Spanish capital Madrid. Current Spain coach Luis de la Fuente was among the mourners, along with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, Atletico Madrid chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin and former Real and Spain coach Jose Antonio Camacho. The family also asked "with the utmost respect, that our privacy - and that of everyone who is supporting us at this time - be respected". "We need to grieve in the peace and quiet that this situation demands," the statement added. "We appreciate the affection, concern and expressions of support that his loss is inspiring, and we are deeply grateful to you all." Players want all matches postponed this weekend The Spanish footballers' union, the AFE, made a request on Thursday for all this weekend's matches to be postponed out of respect for De Miguel. item.title: What new Kane deal means for England and the Premier League record
item.description: England captain Harry Kane scored scored 213 times in 320 league games for Tottenham [Getty Images] Harry Kane's decision to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich carries heavy significance for the Bundesliga giants, who have been celebrating his status as a Ballon d'Or winner, but also for England and the Premier League's record books. Bayern have acted swiftly to secure the 33-year-old on a deal taking him through to 2029 after he was crowned the world's best player, ensuring England's captain and record goalscorer will spend the final peak years of a magnificent career at Allianz Arena. Kane has written himself into Bayern legend since joining from Spurs for £86m in August 2023, scoring 102 goals in 102 Bundesliga matches, winning two league titles and three successive Golden Boot awards. It is why Bayern could not contemplate his departure as other clubs eyed his next move - and why the announcement Kane is staying casts ripples far beyond Munich. Does it mean Kane will never grace the Premier League again? And does it mean - far more enticingly - he has his sights set on two more major tournaments and two more chances to grasp the prize that has eluded him at international level? Former England striker Chris Sutton told BBC Sport: "I certainly think, although you always have to factor fitness issues into all of this, that Harry is more than capable of carrying on for a few years yet, easily. "People might say his game lacks a little bit of pace, but he's so strong in other areas. He is a world-class all-round player. His finishing isn't going to be affected in any way by his age. He can still link up play and his football brain is first class. "I don't see his age being such a big deal. You think of pacy players over the years who rely on that part of the game then lose it as they get older. Harry is not one of those. He seems fit and at the peak of his powers with Bayern and England." Kane's new contract expires shortly before his 36th birthday, certainly raising the prospect the player who left Spurs as the highest scorer in their history with 280 goals in 435 appearances may never grace the Premier League again. His consummate professionalism, and apparent ability to develop into the complete player with age, means this can never be discounted. The notion of an emotional return to Spurs at some point has often provided background noise, but now looks increasingly unlikely. What it surely means is that Alan Shearer will remain the Premier League's highest scorer - who knows what will happen with Erling Haaland as Manchester City await punishment after being found guilty of breaching financial regulations they deny? - and out of Kane's reach. item.title: Ramsey 'loving every second' of being Oxford boss
item.description: Oxford United have lost just one league game this season [Shutterstock] Oxford United boss Aaron Ramsey has admitted he is "loving every second" of his first full coaching role since retiring from playing in April. The Welshman arrived at the Kassam Stadium in June and has impressed across their opening 13 League One games, with the U's one of two sides in the division to have only one defeat this season. On Wednesday, Ramsey's side beat Thames Valley rivals Reading with an impressive performance in a 2-0 victory to move up to third in the standings. Relegated from the Championship last campaign under Gary Rowett and later Matt Bloomfield, United have won seven times with five draws so far and are just three points off the league leaders Huddersfield with a game in hand. "I'm loving every moment of it, me and my staff all credit to them as well," former Arsenal and Wales midfielder Ramsey told BBC Sport. "We work hard to give our players the best opportunities to go out and win football games and we're loving it, I think you can see that as well by the way that we are and the excitement here. "I think the players as well, you can see the way that they respond, they've fully bought into exactly what we demand of them and it's a real pleasure to be here." O'Donkor and Missanga score as Oxford beat Reading Ramsey made 369 appearances for Arsenal across 11 years where he won three FA Cups before moving to Juventus in 2019 where he won the Serie A title and Coppa Italia. In the latter stages of his career, Ramsey played for Nice, returned to boyhood club Cardiff City and made six appearances for Mexican side UNAM Pumas. Before becoming Oxford head coach he spent time as caretaker manager for the Bluebirds at the end of the 2024-25 season. Less than a month after arriving at the Kassam in what was a surprise appointment given his lack of managerial experience, Oxford were placed under a transfer embargo restricting them from signing players. The club were unable to recruit, and lost two key players in Stanley Mills to Preston North End and Brian De Keersmaecker on loan to Bristol City with an option to buy. Despite these departures in the wake of a tough relegation season, the encouraging start under Ramsey has lifted the mood at Oxford with optimism now they can return to the second tier under their new head coach. On Wednesday night, home supporters were chanting Ramsey's name as he leapt into the air and pumped his fist after the victory over the Royals. "Of course, we're proud but we're still early on in the season," Ramsey added. "We go out to win football games and the results and positions and all of that will all take care of itself. "We're not getting carried away or anything, but the boys have bought fully into what we're asking of them and they're producing performances and winning games of football so it's really pleasing for us." item.description: Harry Kane has agreed to a new contract with Bayern Munich -Credit:Alex Grimm, Getty Images Harry Kane has put an end to uncertainty surrounding his future by penning a lucrative new contract with Bayern Munich. Kane, who was recently crowned the Ballon d'Or winner, has prolonged his deal with the German powerhouse until 2029. The agreement is understood to make Kane, 33, Europe's highest-paid player by salary. The England captain's current contract was set to expire at the end of this season. Barcelona expressed interest in signing Kane while former club Tottenham Hotspur had first refusal. But the striker and his family are content in Munich, leading him to commit his future to the Bundesliga champions. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club." Since Bayern paid Spurs £86 million (around $110 million) to acquire Kane in 2023, he's captured five trophies, including two league titles. item.title: Key Scotland duo return for New Zealand rugby clash
item.description: Scotland have been boosted by the return of key duo Sione Tuipulotu and Finn Russell for their Nations Championship clash against New Zealand on Saturday. Neither player featured in Scotland’s previous game, a 33-17 victory over Fiji in July, but both are included in the squad along with several other crucial players. Gregor Brown partner Scott Cummings in the second row and Matt Fagerson is fit enough to start in the back row alongside Rory Darge and former Glasgow Warrior Jack Dempsey. Behind the scrum, Kyle Rowe has been preferred to Blair Kinghorn at fullback, while Huw Jones is favoured over Rory Hutchinson and Stafford McDowall to partner captain Tuipulotu in the midfield. Rory Sutherland starts ahead of Pierre Schoeman and starts at loosehead prop despite only making on appearance for Glasgow this season due to a calf injury. Despite Edinburgh Rubgy’s bright start to the season only hooker Ewan Ashman makes it into the starting XV while there is a landmark appearance for Russell who will win his 100th international cap as he makes his 96th appearance for Scotland, adding to the four Tests he's played for the Lions. Record try-scorer Darcy Graham and wing Duhan van der Merwe have been left out. Saturday's Test kicks off at 2.10pm and is the first of three Nations Championship games at Murrayfield, with Australia and Japan due in the next couple of weeks. Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu returns to the team for the Test against New Zealand (Getty) New Zealand have also named their starting XV for the contest with head coach Dave Rennie making two changes to the team that last faced Australia in Sydney. Ethan de Groot returns at loosehead prop, while Jordie Barrett is back from injury at inside centre. Rennie is expecting a major test at Murrayfield. He said: “Scotland are a quality side. They are very well coached and have built a lot of depth over recent years. item.title: Internacional beat RB Bragantino in women's Copa do Brasil semi opener
item.description: Internacional beat RB Bragantino in women's Copa do Brasil semi opener On Wednesday night (4), Internacional beat Red Bull Bragantino 3–1 to build an important lead in the first leg of the Women’s Copa do Brasil semifinal. The match was played at Beira-Rio in Porto Alegre. Internacional dominated the first half and built a comfortable lead. Valéria Cantuário opened the scoring in the 12th minute, and Lelê found the net in the 29th. Meanwhile, Red Bull Bragantino were kept at bay by Internacional’s defense and struggled to create clear chances. Early in the second half, Sole Jaimes won a penalty after a challenge by goalkeeper Karol Alves and converted it to score Inter’s third. Bragantino kept trying to reduce the deficit. The São Paulo side were also awarded a penalty after a handball by Internacional’s defense, but Miriã sent her effort wide. In stoppage time, Camila Ambrósio pulled one back for Bragantino with a header. The teams meet again on Sunday (8) at 11 a.m. at Cícero de Souza Marques in Bragança Paulista to decide who advances to the Women’s Copa do Brasil final. The other semifinal pits Flamengo against Bahia. The teams played out a goalless draw in the first leg. The return match between the Girls of Gávea and the Women of Steel is scheduled for Saturday (7) at 9:30 p.m. at Estádio Luso-Brasileiro. item.title: A bitter end for Ronaldo - the icon who transformed Portugal
item.description: [BBC] Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him. The Portugal legend has gone another way, and it was always going to be the case. The 41-year-old announced his international retirement after 23 years but also after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus which was resolved with a sanction of 30 days, that had already been served, and a fine of 255 euros. It was the punishment imposed on the Portuguese striker for leaving the team's training camp without permission. Jesus kept him on the bench for one match and said he did not plan to start him in the next, so Ronaldo went home. His last appearance came on 24 September against Wales. He ends his international career with 146 goals in 234 games. A message went around Portugal with a big thank you for everything, calling Ronaldo a global ambassador and an inspiration to millions. Even so, the way it ended leaves a bit of a bitter taste. Was he going to be named in the next squad? Possibly, as Jesus said the door was open and the decision was Ronaldo's. What is clear is that he was no longer an automatic starter, and Cristiano has never handled that well. So is this another hissy fit? Partly, yes. He reacted the way he always has when a coach questions his place. But the label hides how much he adapted over the years. Such a pattern appears with almost every man who sat on the Portuguese bench - there were clashes, but also communion with managers and team-mates that help explain this ending. Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty Ronaldo's most iconic moments as he retires from international football Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast When a young Ronaldo first joined the squad, he arrived at camp with his baseball cap on backwards, enormous sunglasses and headphones turned up so loud they could be heard from a distance. He would not take the cap off to eat among veterans like Luis Figo and Rui Costa. Luiz Felipe Scolari saw an extraordinary player who was immature and obsessed with showing off. He reprimanded him in public, then told him privately that if he changed his attitude, he would one day captain Portugal. The first great disappointment came early, and it came at home. At 19, Ronaldo played in the final of Euro 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a country that had convinced itself the trophy was already on its way. A single headed goal by Angelos Charisteas was enough for unfancied Greece to win it by surprise. When the final whistle went, Ronaldo could not hold back the tears, and the image of the teenager crying on his own pitch travelled everywhere. However, there is a difference between being an outstanding midfielder and becoming a genuine legend, with Steven Gerrard representing a particularly high standard. Rice has time to build a lasting legacy The former Liverpool captain produced iconic performances throughout his career and remains one of the names mentioned when the finest players of his generation are discussed. item.description: Victor Wembanyama is the alien, and on Wednesday night he achieved something that hasn’t been accomplished since shortly after Area 51 was opened. Wemby went off to a level we haven’t see in decades against the Mavericks, finishingwith 52 points, 24 rebounds, and 8 blocks — the first player to hit these marks since Wilt Chamberlain in 1961 . It goes without saying: But everything about this highlight reel shows how unfair the game is. Obviously we’ve known about his length, wingspan, and athleticism since he was touted upon entering the NBA — but the edge he’s added to his game that pushes it into the stratosphere is the amount of poise he’s showing on the defensive end when it comes to blocking shots. We can see in this video that Wemby has developed this technique of hanging on an opponent’s hip and waiting for them to rise for their shot well before he ever jumps. This ensures the shooter’s attempt isn’t altered, as it might be if they jumped at the same time, and Wembanyama knows he can easily match them at the point of release because of his length. item.title: Illinois takes control in second-half, touts Detroit Mercy
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — No. 23 Illinois women’s basketball relied on its frontcourt and overcame a sloppy first half to defeat Detroit Mercy 84-50 on Wednesday night at State Farm Center. Cearah Parchment led Illinois with 22 points, 11 rebounds and four blocks, while Berry Wallace added 21 points and 11 rebounds. The two helped the Illini finish with a 38-22 points-in-the-paint advantage and a 53-23 edge rebounding advantage. “I knew we had to get them there, and it’s hard to stop them when they both get the ball down there,” head coach Shauna Green said. Illinois built a 21-6 lead behind two early Gretchen Dolan 3-pointers and a 14-0 run, but turnovers helped Detroit Mercy work its way back. Illinois committed 15 turnovers before halftime and went the final 4:32 without a field goal, allowing Detroit Mercy to close on a 9-2 run and cut the lead to 36-32. “When we go rogue and start doing our own stuff, it doesn’t end well, and that’s the best film that I have to show them,” Green said. After the half, a Detroit Mercy free throw brought the Titans within three, but afterward, Illinois began to build momentum. The Illini committed just three turnovers after halftime and outscored Detroit Mercy 48-18 over the final two quarters. “So the pace didn’t change,” Green said. “We just made better decisions within the pace.” Wallace scored 11 points in the third quarter, including a 3-pointer that started a 14-0 run to close the period. Parchment scored two early layups in the fourth, as well as converted a three-point play to extend the lead to 29. Wallace and Parchment became the first Illinois women’s teammates to record 20-point double-doubles in the same game since Karisma Penn and Adrienne GodBold in February 2013. “I think it’s just dangerous because we’re both so versatile,” Parchment said of playing alongside Wallace. “We can both shoot, we can both post up.” Illinois also turned its rebound advantage into 18 second-chance points, doubling the nine of Detroit Mercy. Dolan finished with 10 points, while Aaliyah Guyton scored nine and Destiny Jackson contributed seven points, as well as nine assists. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s long Portugal goodbye leaves complicated legacy
item.description: It could be called the long goodbye, although really it was an extremely long goodbye . The beginning of the end came in Qatar, in December 2022, when Portugal beat Switzerland 6-1, with a Goncalo Ramos hat-trick . Cristiano Ronaldo took almost four years to take a hint. His retirement from international football came three months before his 42nd birthday, more than 23 years after his debut and two major tournaments too late. The undignified finish felt sadly inevitable. There was to be no happy ending: not when Portugal’s chances of winning Euro 2024 or the 2026 World Cup were fatally wounded by picking Ronaldo. So instead the world’s second oldest toddler – it has not been a good week for ageing egomaniacs on either side of the Atlantic – ended up bidding farewell to his country by flouncing out of the camp last month after being left an unused substitute against Norway, wanting manager Jorge Jesus to apologise for “putting someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game”, in his own words, posting a self-pitying, self-important 2,000-word opus on Instagram. Ronaldo’s 30-day suspension from the Portuguese FA is as irrelevant as the much-mocked £215 fine ; the real punishment for a billionaire is the eventual recognition that he cannot carry on for Portugal forever. Cristiano Ronaldo’s legacy is complicated but he’s undoubtedly Portugal’s greatest player (Reuters) And the final chapter should not obscure what an astonishing career it has been. The numbers are beefed up by the last four years, but Ronaldo’s 234 caps and 146 goals are records in international football, and should remain so for quite some time. Astonishingly, he is 99 goals clear of Portugal’s second top scorer, Pauleta. Between them, Luis Figo and Eusebio scored half as many goals for their country as he did. For a long time, Eusebio’s status as Portugal’s greatest footballer went unchallenged. Now it is clear he stands in second place. The last four years mean some of the statistics need qualifying. Ronaldo is Portugal’s record scorer in world cups, but it was only in the sixth that he passed Eusebio, who played in one. He is the only man to score in six World Cups, but the fact that only one of those goals came in a knockout game, and that was a penalty in a last-32 match, means he underwhelmed on the global stage. Yet he can nevertheless be called the greatest player in the history of the European Championships; with 30 appearances and 14 goals. He is the only Portugal captain to lift a major trophy, and while he went off injured in the final of Euro 2016, the sight of Ronaldo on the sidelines, part coach, part super-fan, is one of the indelible images of his two decades of international football. item.title: Steelers QB Mason Rudolph listed as possible trade candidate
item.description: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers were one of only a handful of teams to keep four quarterbacks on their final 53-man rosters back in August. Most expected this, but it leaves the Steelers in a peculiar position with two veteran options on expiring contracts and two young fliers developing behind the scenes. Is it all possible Pittsburgh considers moving a quarterback at the deadline with a laundry list of injuries around the league? It’s not crazy to ask, in fact, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN listed the veteran quarterback as a potential trade candidate ahead of next week’s deadline. “Quarterback Mason Rudolph,” Fowler wrote. “The Steelers are more likely to bring in players at the deadline. In fact, I don’t expect Pittsburgh to move anyone. But it has a surplus at quarterback, and should more quarterback injuries occur around the league, perhaps teams call on Rudolph with an attractive offer.” Rudolph has started just one game over the course of the last two seasons for Pittsburgh. It’s important to keep in mind that this is simply speculation, and Fowler even says that he doesn’t expect Pittsburgh to move anyone. It would not make much sense for the Steelers to move a veteran quarterback like Rudolph who they have familiarity with and confidence in that he can run the offense and win some games should Aaron Rodgers miss time. However, crazier things have happened. Who’s to say the Steelers won’t get an offer for Rudolph that they can’t refuse? At 6-2 overall with sole possession of first place in the AFC North, it could be a very active next few days in the trade market for general manager Omar Khan and his Steelers.
